newsitem.title: USA: Clinton plan has $45 bln hospital savings -- W.House.
newsitem.headline: Clinton plan has $45 bln hospital savings -- W.House.

text.p: President Bill Clinton's plan to save $138 billion in Medicare savings includes $45 billion in savings from hospitals over six years and $40 billion in managed care savings, the White House said Tuesday.

Gene Sperling, Clinton's National Economic Council chairman, said the managed care savings would reverse what he called an overpayment to doctors. Medicare fee-for-services payments to Health Maintenance Organizations would be reduced to 90 percent from the current 95 percent, he said.

The plan would save $20 billion over six years through the implementation of a new payment system and initiatives against fraud and abuse, Sperling said. There will also be $10 billion in Medicare Part B savings brought about by extending the stipulation that 25 percent of costs be covered by premiums.
Presidential aides said the $138 billion over six years in Medicare savings moves closer to the Republicans' recommendation of $158 billion over six years made last year.
"There is substantial movement here and it is the result of taking tough policy decisions in an effort to balance the budget," said Health and Human Services Secretary Donna Shalala.
